description: The SEO article readers as typed questions. Every question is true when there is a problem, so a high probability always means the same thing. The brief and the source list belong in the state's input field; the section's prose in output.

claim-outside-brief.instructions: This sentence makes a factual claim that nothing in the research brief supports.

criteria.true: The sentence asserts something about the world that the brief in the state does not contain.
criteria.false: Everything the sentence asserts is in the brief, is a definition of a term the brief uses, or is a transition that asserts nothing.

figure-uncited.instructions: This sentence gives a number that no bracketed citation marker supports.

criteria.true: A figure, a percentage, a money amount, a count appears with no bracketed marker such as [3] attached to the sentence.
criteria.false: The sentence has no figure in it, or every figure in it sits in a sentence carrying a bracketed marker.

named-study-uncited.instructions: This sentence names a study whose bracketed citation marker is missing.

criteria.true: A named report, survey, index, publisher is referred to with no bracketed marker attached to the sentence.
criteria.false: No named study appears, or the named study carries its marker.

jargon-term.instructions: This sentence uses a term that the owner of a small business would not recognise.

criteria.true: A term of art appears with no plain explanation beside it.
criteria.false: Every term in the sentence is ordinary business language, is a proper name, is explained where it appears.

heading-answered.instructions: The opening sentence of this section leaves the question in its heading unanswered.

criteria.true: A reader who read the heading, then the first sentence, still does not have the answer.
criteria.false: The first sentence gives the answer the heading promises.

keyword-natural.instructions: A use of the primary keyword in this text reads as forced.

criteria.true: At least one occurrence of the keyword sits in a sentence no writer would have written that way.
criteria.false: Every occurrence reads as ordinary prose.
